ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

2. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a describing word

4. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. blue

5. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

6. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. went

8. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

9. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

10. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

11. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

12. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Listening Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

3. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. C — run

5. B — Where is the library?

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

7. D — went

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

9. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Listening Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
